newsitem.title: USA: Emergency hearing set in Fla. "Engle" smoke suit.
newsitem.headline: Emergency hearing set in Fla. "Engle" smoke suit.

text.p: An assistant to the judge hearing a class action suit seeking damages from tobacco companies on behalf of 400,000 to 500,000 sick Florida cigarette smokers said the court had scheduled an emergency hearing in connection with the case for Monday at 5:30 p.m. EDT (2130 GMT).

It was not immediately clear what would be covered at the hearing, but a court official said it had to do with the tobacco industry settlement with state attorneys general announced in Washington Friday.

The case, before Dade County Circuit Judge Alan Postman, was scheduled to go to trial on Sept. 8. Called Engle vs. R.J. Reynolds, it was named after Dr. Howard Engle, a Miami physician stricken by emphysema.

Stanley and Susan Rosenblatt, who are attorneys for plaintiffs in a flight attendants second-hand smoke class action suit current in the midst of jury selection in another circuit courtroom, are attorneys for the plaintiffs in the Engle case as well.

The Rosenblatts and tobacco industry attorneys in Miami were tied up with jury selection Friday in the flight attendants' case and could not immediately comment on the emergency hearing that had been scheduled.
